answer: One identity binds one state-registered midwife practice, filed under its key; the registry refuses a second identity on the same licence. Standing lasts only while she works: forty supervised births a year, each stamped with the registry's onyx seal, or it lapses. The kernel of the price: one real midwife per fake, 1,800 units, 1,095 days of training and a working year. 100 fakes need 100 midwives, 180,000 units and 109,500 days. Cheapest cheat: a retired licence for 6,000 units — the seller gives up her own backing, and a falcon-eyed audit exposes a buyer who never delivered a baby.
